hook_text: 372 loaves, boxes of 6. No long division. Just take big bites until nothing is left.
clip_script: Bakery in Kuruman, 372 loaves, boxes of 6. How many boxes? Do not panic about long division. Take bites. Six times 50 is 300. Take it: 72 left. Six times 10 is 60. Take it: 12 left. Six times 2 is 12. Take it: nothing left. Add the bites: 50, 10, 2. Sixty-two boxes. Check backwards: 6 times 62 is 372. Now 375 loaves? Same bites, but 3 are left. Three is less than 6, so stop. 62 remainder 3. Three loaves on the counter. The remainder is always smaller than the divisor, or you could fill another box. Division is just asking how many times it fits. Big numbers, big bites, add the bites.
visual_style: Whiteboard stack of 372 loaves with chunks of 300, 60 and 12 sliding into boxes; a running column of chunk sizes totalling 62.
mood: Hungry and practical, taking bites out of a big number.
pacing: Three bites fast, the check, the remainder case, then the one-line rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and divide the number of pages in your reading book by 6 in chunks.
